LESSON: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: DIARY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we plan our activities in advance?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal
2. create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: DIARY
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: DIARY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format

What this means
In this part you learn to create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary to a partner. (skill: create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal.
3. Practise this skill: create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we plan our activities in advance?
2. What is the most memorable experience in your life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: Diary means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the key components of a diary/journal from a sample diary/journal.
5. Be able to: create a journal/diary to convey desired information in the right format.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
